examples.en: My lower lip turned blue from the cold.
I have a habit of biting my lower lip when I'm nervous.

examples.ko: 김 씨가 아랫입술을 비죽이 내밀고 저를 쳐다봤어요.
examples.en: Mr. Kim pushed out his lower lip and looked at me.
I hurt my lower lip when I fell, and it bled.

examples.ko: 아랫입술이 터져서 밥 먹을 때 아파요.
examples.en: My lower lip is cracked, so it hurts when I eat.

examples.ko: 자기 전에 아랫입술에 립밤을 듬뿍 발랐어요.
examples.en: I put a lot of lip balm on my lower lip before bed.

explain: 반대말은 '윗입술'이에요. 삐졌거나 울 것 같을 때 '아랫입술을 내밀다', 참거나 긴장할 때 '아랫입술을 깨물다'처럼 표정이나 버릇을 말할 때 자주 써요.
explain_en: The opposite is '윗입술' (upper lip). It often appears in expressions of mood or habit, such as '아랫입술을 내밀다' when sulking, or '아랫입술을 깨물다' when holding back or feeling tense.

examples.ko: 날이 더워서 아이스티 한 잔 시켰어요.
examples.en: It was hot, so I ordered an iced tea.
I put a slice of lemon in my iced tea.
I drink iced tea instead of coffee.

examples.ko: 아이스티가 너무 달아서 물을 조금 더 탔어요.
examples.en: The iced tea was too sweet, so I added a little more water.

examples.ko: 편의점에서 캔 아이스티를 두 개 샀어요.
examples.en: I bought two cans of iced tea at the convenience store.
Have you ever made iced tea at home yourself?

explain: 카페에서는 '아이스'와 '핫'으로 나눠서 주문해요. 가루를 물에 타서 마시는 복숭아 맛 음료도 보통 '아이스티'라고 불러요.
explain_en: At cafés you order either 'ice' or 'hot'. A peach-flavored drink made by mixing powder with water is also commonly called '아이스티'.

examples.ko: 아이큐 검사를 받았는데 결과가 꽤 높게 나왔어요.
examples.en: I took an IQ test and the result came out quite high.
I heard that child's IQ is over 150.

examples.ko: 아이큐와 공부 성적은 꼭 비례하지는 않아요.
examples.en: IQ and school grades don't necessarily go together.

examples.ko: 어렸을 때 학교에서 아이큐 테스트를 한 적이 있어요.
examples.en: I once took an IQ test at school when I was little.

examples.ko: 아이큐가 높다고 다 행복한 건 아니에요.
examples.en: Having a high IQ doesn't mean everyone is happy.

examples.ko: 퀴즈 프로그램에서 아이큐가 높은 사람들이 문제를 풀었어요.
examples.en: On the quiz show, people with high IQs solved the problems.

explain: 'IQ'라고 영어로 쓰기도 해요. '지능지수'가 정식 말이고, 일상 대화에서는 '아이큐'라고 많이 말해요. '높다/낮다'와 자주 함께 써요.
explain_en: It is often written in English as 'IQ'. '지능지수' is the formal term, while people usually say '아이큐' in daily talk. It commonly goes with '높다' (high) and '낮다' (low).

en: temples of a pair of spectacles

examples.en: My glasses' temple broke yesterday, so I taped it.

examples.ko: 안경다리가 너무 꽉 조여서 귀 뒤가 아파요.
examples.en: The temples are so tight that the area behind my ears hurts.
I bent the temples slightly to fit my face.
The child keeps grabbing and pulling the temples of my glasses.

examples.ko: 이 안경은 안경다리 색이 예뻐서 마음에 들어요.
examples.en: I like these glasses because the temples are a pretty color.

examples.ko: 안경다리 안쪽에 작은 글씨로 상표가 적혀 있어요.
examples.en: The brand name is written in small letters on the inside of the temple.

explain: 안경에서 귀에 거는 긴 부분이에요. 앞에서 렌즈를 감싸는 부분은 '안경테'라고 해서 서로 구별해요. 안경이 헐거울 때는 '안경다리를 조이다'라고 말해요.
explain_en: This is the long part of glasses that goes over the ear. The part that holds the lenses at the front is called '안경테', so the two are distinguished. When glasses are loose, people say '안경다리를 조이다'.

examples.ko: 한쪽 렌즈에 금이 가서 안경점에 갔어요.
examples.en: One lens cracked, so I went to the optician's.
My sunglasses lens got scratched, so I had it replaced at the optician's.

examples.ko: 집 근처 안경점이 오늘은 문을 닫았어요.
examples.en: The optician's near my home is closed today.

examples.ko: 안경점에서 시력을 재고 새 안경을 맞췄어요.
examples.en: I had my eyesight tested and ordered new glasses at the optician's.

examples.ko: 안경점 사장님이 안경테를 친절하게 골라 주셨어요.
examples.en: The owner of the optician's kindly helped me choose frames.
My glasses got loose, so I stopped by the optician's to have them adjusted.

explain: 안경을 맞추는 것뿐 아니라 렌즈를 갈거나 안경다리를 조이는 것도 안경점에서 해 줘요. 가게 이름에는 '안경원'이라는 말을 쓰는 곳도 있어요.
explain_en: Besides ordering glasses, you can also get lenses replaced or temples tightened at an '안경점'. Some shops use the name '안경원' instead.

examples.en: These frames are thin, so they're light and comfortable.
I changed the frame color from black to brown.

examples.ko: 얼굴이 둥글어서 각진 안경테가 잘 어울려요.
examples.en: My face is round, so angular frames suit me well.
The frame was bent, so I took it to the optician's.

examples.ko: 안경테만 새로 사고 렌즈는 그대로 썼어요.
examples.en: I bought only new frames and kept the same lenses.
Expensive frames don't break easily.

explain: 렌즈(안경알)를 제외한 틀 부분이에요. 귀에 거는 부분은 따로 '안경다리'라고 불러요. 안경을 고를 때는 '테'와 '렌즈'를 따로 골라요.
explain_en: It is the frame part of glasses, without the lenses ('안경알'). The part that goes over the ears is called '안경다리' separately. When buying glasses, you choose the frame and the lenses separately.

examples.ko: 새 제품의 안전성에 대해 소비자들이 의문을 제기하고 있어요.
examples.en: Consumers are raising questions about the safety of the new product.

examples.ko: 차를 고를 때 첫째는 가격이고 둘째로는 안전성을 봤어요.
examples.en: When choosing a car, price came first and safety second.
This toy passed the safety inspection.

examples.ko: 약은 효과도 중요하지만 안전성이 더 중요해요.
examples.en: Effectiveness matters for medicine, but safety matters even more.

examples.ko: 아이 카시트는 무엇보다 안전성이 가장 중요해요.
examples.en: For a child's car seat, safety is the most important thing.
They say they will delay sales until the safety is confirmed.

explain: 제품, 약, 기술, 시설이 얼마나 안전한지 평가할 때 써요. 사람이나 장소가 안전할 때는 그냥 '안전해요'라고 말해요. 반대말은 '위험성'이에요.
explain_en: It is used when evaluating how safe a product, medicine, technology or facility is. For a person or place, people simply say '안전해요'. The opposite is '위험성' (riskiness).

examples.ko: 차가 오자 도로 한가운데 안전지대로 피했어요.
examples.en: When a car came, I moved to the safety zone in the middle of the road.
I waited in the safety zone in front of the bus stop.
These days nowhere is a completely safe zone.

examples.ko: 이 지역은 홍수 걱정이 없는 안전지대예요.
examples.en: This area is a safe zone where there is no worry about floods.

examples.ko: 길 가운데 안전지대에 서서 신호를 기다렸어요.
examples.en: I stood on the safety island in the middle of the road and waited for the signal.

examples.ko: 비가 많이 와도 우리 마을은 안전지대예요.
examples.en: Even when it rains a lot, our village is a safe zone.

explain: 도로 가운데 사람이 잠시 피해 서 있는 구역이라는 실제 장소도 가리키고, 위험이 없는 곳이라는 비유로도 많이 써요. 비유로 쓸 때는 '어디도 안전지대가 아니다'처럼 부정문에 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It can mean an actual spot in the middle of a road where people can stand safely, and it is also widely used figuratively for a place free of danger. In the figurative sense it often appears in negatives like '어디도 안전지대가 아니다' (nowhere is safe).

examples.en: Grandmother took a hard candy out of her pocket and gave it to me.

examples.ko: 알사탕을 입에 물고 있으면 볼이 볼록해져요.
examples.en: When you hold a round candy in your mouth, your cheek bulges.

examples.ko: 아이가 알사탕 하나에 금방 기분이 풀렸어요.
examples.en: The child cheered up right away with just one candy.

examples.ko: 알사탕은 오래 녹여 먹을 수 있어서 좋아요.
examples.en: I like round candies because you can enjoy them for a long time.
I bought three round candies at the stationery store.

examples.ko: 알사탕이 너무 커서 한 번에 못 먹겠어요.
examples.en: The candy is so big that I can't eat it all at once.

explain: '사탕' 중에서도 동글동글한 알 모양의 딱딱한 사탕을 가리켜요. 막대 모양 사탕과 구별해서 말할 때 쓰고, 보통 깨물지 않고 입에서 녹여 먹어요.
explain_en: Among '사탕' (candy), it specifically means the hard, round, ball-shaped kind. It is used to tell it apart from lollipop-type candy, and people usually let it dissolve in the mouth instead of biting it.

examples.en: I let the steam out of the pressure cooker and opened the lid.

examples.ko: 압력솥으로 밥을 하면 훨씬 빨리 돼요.
examples.en: Cooking rice in a pressure cooker is much faster.
The pressure cooker started making a hissing sound.
If you make braised ribs in a pressure cooker, the meat gets tender.
My mother boiled potatoes in the pressure cooker.

examples.ko: 압력솥 뚜껑이 안 열려서 한참 기다렸어요.
examples.en: The pressure cooker lid wouldn't open, so I waited a long time.

explain: '밥솥'은 밥을 짓는 솥이고, '압력솥'은 압력으로 음식을 빨리 익히는 솥이라 찜이나 삶는 요리에도 써요. '김'은 뜨거운 수증기를 뜻해서 '김이 나다', '김을 빼다'처럼 말해요.
explain_en: A '밥솥' is a pot for cooking rice, while a '압력솥' cooks food quickly under pressure, so it is also used for braising and boiling. Here '김' means hot steam, as in '김이 나다' (steam comes out) and '김을 빼다' (let the steam out).

examples.en: I made kimchi stew with pork foreleg meat.

examples.ko: 고양이가 앞다리를 쭉 뻗고 기지개를 켰어요.
examples.en: The cat stretched out its front legs and had a good stretch.
The puppy scratched my knee with its front paw.
The horse raised its front legs and neighed loudly.
A rabbit's hind legs are much longer than its front legs.
Since falling, the puppy has been limping on its front leg.

explain: 주로 동물의 앞쪽 다리를 말하고, 반대말은 '뒷다리'예요. 사람의 팔은 '앞다리'라고 하지 않고 '팔'이라고 해요. 요리에서는 '앞다리살'이라는 고기 부위 이름으로도 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It mainly means the front legs of an animal, and the opposite is '뒷다리'. A person's arm is just called '팔', not '앞다리'. It also appears often in cooking as the meat cut '앞다리살'.

examples.en: The children are playing ball in the front yard.
There is a persimmon tree in the front yard of my grandmother's house.
When spring comes, we plant flowers in the front yard.
I feel refreshed after sweeping the front yard.
The puppy runs around happily in the front yard.
We made a small vegetable patch in the front yard of our house.

explain: 집 앞쪽에 있는 뜰이고, 반대말은 '뒤뜰'이에요. 단독 주택이나 시골집 이야기에서 주로 나오고, 일반적으로 집 앞 공간은 '마당'이라고도 해요.
explain_en: It is the garden in front of a house, and the opposite is '뒤뜰' (backyard). It mostly appears when talking about detached houses or country homes, and the open space in front of a house is also generally called '마당'.

examples.ko: 나가기 전에 거울로 내 앞모습을 확인했어요.
examples.en: Before going out, I checked my front view in the mirror.

examples.ko: 앞모습은 멋있는데 뒷모습은 어딘가 피곤해 보여요.
examples.en: He looks cool from the front, but from behind he looks somehow tired.

examples.ko: 사진 속 앞모습만 보고는 누군지 몰랐어요.
examples.en: I couldn't tell who it was just from the front view in the photo.
From the front, he looks a lot like his father.
The front of the building was pretty, so I took a photo.

examples.ko: 뒷모습만 보고 아는 사람인 줄 알았는데 앞모습을 보고 깜짝 놀랐어요.
examples.en: I thought it was someone I knew from the back, but I was startled when I saw the front.

explain: 반대말은 '뒷모습'이에요. 사람의 얼굴이나 앞쪽 모양, 건물의 앞쪽 모양에 써요. '뒷모습'은 쓸쓸하거나 믿음직한 느낌을 말할 때 자주 써요.
explain_en: The opposite is '뒷모습' (back view). It is used for a person's face or front appearance and for the front of a building. '뒷모습' is often used to describe a lonely or reliable feeling.

examples.ko: 앞사람 머리 때문에 영화 화면이 안 보여요.
examples.en: I can't see the movie screen because of the head of the person in front of me.
The person ahead stopped suddenly and I almost bumped into them.

examples.ko: 줄을 설 때는 앞사람과 거리를 두세요.
examples.en: When standing in line, keep some distance from the person in front.
I followed the person ahead and walked in slowly.
After the person ahead got off, I sat down.
When the person before me finishes talking, I'll ask my question too.

explain: 줄이나 자리, 순서에서 바로 앞에 있는 사람을 말하고, 반대말은 '뒷사람'이에요. 보통 줄 서기, 극장 좌석, 발표 순서 같은 상황에서 써요.
explain_en: It means the person right in front of you in a line, seat or order, and the opposite is '뒷사람'. It typically comes up in situations like queuing, theater seats and speaking order.

en: go ahead; go before; take the lead

examples.ko: 친구가 저보다 몇 걸음 앞서가고 있어요.
examples.en: My friend is a few steps ahead of me.
Our team stayed in the lead until the second half.

examples.ko: 그 회사는 기술에서 다른 회사보다 앞서가요.
examples.en: That company is ahead of other companies in technology.
I walked along the road following the person ahead.

examples.ko: 아이가 혼자 앞서가서 자꾸 불러야 했어요.
examples.en: The child kept going ahead alone, so I had to keep calling out.

examples.ko: 시대를 앞서가는 생각이라서 처음엔 이해하기 어려웠어요.
examples.en: It was a thought ahead of its time, so it was hard to understand at first.

explain: '앞서다'와 비슷하지만 '앞서가다'는 실제로 먼저 걸어가거나 앞에서 이끄는 느낌이 있어요. 기술이나 생각이 남보다 낫다고 할 때도 써요. 반대로 뒤에 처지는 것은 '뒤처지다'라고 해요.
explain_en: It is similar to '앞서다', but '앞서가다' carries more of a feeling of actually walking ahead or leading from the front. It is also used when technology or ideas are better than others'. The opposite, falling behind, is '뒤처지다'.

examples.en: I sliced the squash thinly and put it in the soybean paste stew.
My mother made squash pancakes for me.

examples.ko: 애호박이 싱싱해서 마트에서 두 개 샀어요.
examples.en: The squash was fresh, so I bought two at the supermarket.
I stir-fried the squash and ate it as a side dish.
Young squash is softer and more tender than old pumpkin.
One squash is enough to make soup.

explain: 덜 자란 어린 호박이라서 껍질이 얇고 부드러워요. 다 익어 단단해진 '늙은호박'과 구별해요. 주키니와 비슷하게 쓰이지만 한국 요리에서는 전, 찌개, 볶음에 자주 넣어요.
explain_en: It is an immature, young pumpkin, so the skin is thin and soft. It is distinguished from the fully ripened, hard '늙은호박'. It is used similarly to zucchini, and in Korean cooking it often goes into pancakes, stews and stir-fries.

examples.en: I went to a campground with my family on the weekend.
I like this campground because the shower rooms are clean.
In summer, campground reservations fill up quickly.
We pitched a tent at the campground and grilled meat.
There is a valley stream near the campground, so it's cool.

examples.ko: 야영장 이용 요금은 하룻밤에 삼만 원이에요.
examples.en: The campground fee is thirty thousand won per night.

explain: 일상 대화에서는 '캠핑장'이라고 더 자주 말하는 편이에요. 안내문이나 공식적인 글에서는 '야영장'이 많이 보여요. 두 말은 뜻이 같아요.
explain_en: In everyday conversation people tend to say '캠핑장' more. In notices and official writing you often see '야영장'. The two words mean the same thing.

examples.en: Palm trees stand in a row on the beach.
I rested for a moment in the shade of a palm tree.
They planted palm trees in the hotel garden.
The palm leaves are swaying in the wind.
Many palm trees grow in tropical regions.

examples.ko: 그림 속 야자수가 휴양지 느낌을 줘요.
examples.en: The palm tree in the picture gives a resort feel.

explain: '야자나무'라고도 해요. 야자수는 바다, 휴가, 열대 같은 느낌을 떠올리게 해서 그림이나 인테리어에서도 자주 쓰여요.
explain_en: It is also called '야자나무'. Palm trees bring to mind the sea, vacations and the tropics, so they are often used in pictures and interior decoration.

examples.ko: 약방에서 붕대를 사다가 상처 난 곳에 감았어요.
examples.en: I bought a bandage at the drugstore and wrapped it around the wound.

examples.ko: 어릴 때 동네 약방에서 감기약을 샀어요.
examples.en: When I was little, I bought cold medicine at the neighborhood drugstore.
My grandfather is old friends with the man at the drugstore.
Old drugstores were full of the smell of herbal medicine.
The drugstore is closed, so I plan to go tomorrow.

examples.ko: 요즘은 약방보다 약국이라는 말을 더 많이 써요.
examples.en: These days people say yakguk more than yakbang.

explain: 요즘은 보통 '약국'이라고 하고, '약방'은 옛날 느낌이나 한약을 파는 가게 느낌이 있어요. 지금 동네 가게를 말할 때는 '약국'이 자연스러워요.

phrases.example: 그 배우는 어느 드라마에나 나오는 약방의 감초예요.
phrases.en: That actor is the one who shows up in every drama.
phrases.nuance_ko: 한약에 감초가 거의 늘 들어가는 데서 나온 말로, 어디에나 빠지지 않고 끼는 사람이나 물건을 말해요. 좋은 뜻으로 쓸 때가 많지만 참견하는 사람에게도 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Coming from licorice root being added to almost every herbal remedy, it describes a person or thing that is part of everything. It is often positive but can also be used for someone who gets involved in everything.
phrases.en_equiv: a fixture; someone who's in everything

explain_en: Today people usually say '약국', while '약방' has an old-fashioned feel or suggests a shop selling herbal medicine. For a neighborhood shop today, '약국' sounds more natural.

examples.en: My younger sibling was born in the year of the sheep.
I'm a sheep, what is your zodiac animal, teacher?
My mother is the only sheep in our family.
I have many friends born in the year of the sheep.
We sheep-year people decided to get together for dinner.
I went to the sheep-year gathering for the first time in a while.

explain: '띠'는 태어난 해를 나타내는 십이지 동물이에요. 한국에서는 '무슨 띠예요?'라고 물어서 상대의 나이를 짐작하기도 해요. 같은 띠인 사람은 열두 살 차이가 나요.
explain_en: '띠' is the zodiac animal of the year you were born. In Korea people sometimes ask '무슨 띠예요?' to guess someone's age. People with the same zodiac animal are twelve years apart.

examples.ko: 길 양편에 벚꽃나무가 쭉 늘어서 있어요.
examples.en: Cherry trees line both sides of the road.

examples.ko: 두 사람은 서로 양편으로 갈라져 앉았어요.
examples.en: The two people sat apart on opposite sides.

examples.ko: 양편의 이야기를 다 들어 봐야 해요.
examples.en: You have to hear both sides of the story.
There is one village on each side of the river.
I hope both sides each give a little.
Security guards are standing on both sides of the door.

explain: '양쪽'과 거의 같아요. '편'이 들어가서 의견이나 입장이 갈린 두 쪽을 말할 때 특히 자연스러워요. 위치를 말할 때는 '길 양쪽'처럼 '양쪽'도 많이 써요.
explain_en: It is nearly the same as '양쪽'. Because it contains '편' (side/team), it is especially natural when talking about two sides with different opinions or positions. For location, '양쪽' is also widely used, as in '길 양쪽'.

examples.ko: 머리가 아파서 양호실에 가서 누워 있었어요.
examples.en: My head hurt, so I went to the nurse's office and lay down.
The nurse's office teacher got medicine for me.
I fell during gym class and went to the nurse's office.

examples.ko: 양호실에는 침대 두 개가 놓여 있어요.
examples.en: There are two beds in the nurse's office.

examples.ko: 열이 나면 먼저 양호실에 가 보세요.
examples.en: If you have a fever, go to the nurse's office first.
After resting a little in the nurse's office, I felt better.

explain: 학교에서 아픈 학생을 돌보는 방이에요. 요즘 학교에서는 '보건실'이라고 많이 불러요. 같은 장소를 가리키는 말이라서 어른들은 옛날 말인 '양호실'을 쓰기도 해요.
explain_en: It is the room at school where sick students are looked after. Schools today often call it '보건실'. It refers to the same place, and adults sometimes still use the older word '양호실'.

examples.en: Oh my, you scared me! When did you get here?

examples.ko: 어이구, 허리야. 오래 앉아 있었더니 아파요.
examples.en: Ouch, my back. It hurts from sitting for so long.
Oh my, our puppy has grown so much.
Oh no, did you spill your coffee again?

examples.ko: 어이구, 이렇게 무거운 걸 혼자 들었어요?
examples.en: Oh my, you carried something this heavy alone?

examples.ko: 어이구, 어제 밤새 일하느라 고생 많았어요.
examples.en: Oh dear, you had a hard time working all night yesterday.

explain: 놀람, 아픔, 귀여움, 안쓰러움, 어이없음 같은 여러 감정을 한마디로 나타내요. '아이고'와 비슷하게 쓰고, 어른들이 말할 때 자주 들려요. 같은 말이라도 목소리 톤에 따라 느낌이 달라져요.
explain_en: It expresses various feelings in one word, such as surprise, pain, cuteness, sympathy or disbelief. It is used much like '아이고' and is often heard from older people. The feeling changes depending on your tone of voice.

examples.en: I stood up suddenly and felt dizzy, so I sat down.
If the dizziness continues, go see a doctor.
I feel dizzy every morning, so I'm worried.
I get severe dizziness when I ride a boat.
I left work early today because of dizziness.
After taking medicine, the dizziness calmed down a lot.

explain: '어지럽다'에서 나온 말이에요. 말할 때는 '어지러워요'라고 하는 경우가 많고, 병원에서 증상을 설명하거나 글로 쓸 때 '어지럼증'이 자주 나와요. '어지럼증이 나다/생기다/있다'와 잘 어울려요.
explain_en: It comes from '어지럽다' (to be dizzy). In speech people often just say '어지러워요', while '어지럼증' appears often when describing symptoms at a hospital or in writing. It goes well with '어지럼증이 나다/생기다/있다'.

examples.en: Anyway, we have to finish it today.
Anyway, I'm glad you arrived safely.
Anyway, let's meet once and talk.

examples.ko: 이유가 뭐든 어쨌건 약속은 지켜야 해요.
examples.en: Whatever the reason, you have to keep your promise anyway.
Anyway, I agree with this plan.
Anyway, the exam is over, so get some good rest.

explain: '어쨌든'과 뜻이 같아서 바꿔 쓸 수 있어요. 앞의 이야기는 접어 두고 중요한 결론이나 본론으로 돌아갈 때 써요. 문장 맨 앞에 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It has the same meaning as '어쨌든' and the two can be swapped. It is used to set aside what came before and return to the main point or conclusion. It often comes at the start of a sentence.

examples.en: That player receives a salary of over a hundred million won.
I have debts in the hundred-million range, so my heart is heavy.
These days in Seoul, jeonse deposits of over a hundred million won are common.
News of a contract worth over a hundred million won came out.
I heard there are even YouTubers earning over a hundred million won.

examples.ko: 그 집은 억대를 훌쩍 넘는 가격이에요.
examples.en: That house is priced well over a hundred million won.

explain: '억' 단위의 큰 돈을 말해요. 원 단위로 보면 1억 원부터 9억 원대까지를 뜻하고, '억대 연봉', '억대 계약'처럼 자주 써요. 돈이 더 크면 '십억대'나 '조 단위'처럼 말해요.
explain_en: It refers to large sums in the unit of '억' (hundred million). In won, that is from 100 million up to the 900-million range, as in '억대 연봉' (salary in the hundred-million range) and '억대 계약'. For larger amounts people say '십억대' or '조 단위'.

examples.ko: 두 나라 사이에는 언어적 차이가 커요.
examples.en: There is a big linguistic difference between the two countries.
That child has outstanding linguistic talent.
At first it was hard because of the language barrier.

examples.ko: 언어적 표현보다 몸짓이 더 잘 통할 때도 있어요.
examples.en: Sometimes gestures work better than verbal expression.

examples.ko: 언어적 능력은 어릴 때 많이 자라요.
examples.en: Language ability grows a lot when you are young.
This problem is hard to explain in words.

explain: 뒤에 명사가 와서 '언어적 차이', '언어적 장벽'처럼 써요. 반대로 몸짓이나 표정 같은 것은 '비언어적'이라고 해요. '언어적으로'처럼 쓰면 '말이나 언어의 면에서'라는 느낌이에요.
explain_en: It comes before a noun, as in '언어적 차이' and '언어적 장벽'. Things like gestures and facial expressions are called '비언어적' (nonverbal). Used as '언어적으로', it means 'in terms of language or words'.

examples.ko: 얼굴색이 안 좋아 보이는데 어디 아파요?
examples.en: You look pale, are you sick somewhere?
When I put on makeup, my complexion gets much brighter.

examples.ko: 이 옷은 얼굴색을 환하게 만들어 줘요.
examples.en: This outfit makes my complexion look bright.

examples.ko: 그 소식을 듣고 얼굴색이 확 바뀌었어요.
examples.en: His face changed color when he heard the news.
I got a lot of sun, so my complexion changed.
I chose a lipstick that matches my skin tone.

explain: 건강이나 기분이 드러나는 얼굴의 색을 말해요. '얼굴색이 안 좋다'는 아프거나 피곤해 보인다는 걱정의 말로 자주 써요. 화장품이나 옷 이야기에서는 피부 톤을 뜻하기도 해요.
explain_en: It means the color of the face, which shows health or mood. '얼굴색이 안 좋다' is often said out of concern when someone looks sick or tired. In talk about cosmetics or clothes, it can also mean skin tone.

examples.ko: 저는 얼굴형이 동그래서 짧은 머리가 잘 어울려요.
examples.en: My face is round, so short hair suits me well.
I chose frames that match my face shape.
My face is slim, so I wore bangs.
The two of them have very similar face shapes.

examples.ko: 얼굴형에 따라 어울리는 머리 모양이 달라요.
examples.en: The hairstyle that suits you differs depending on your face shape.
I have an angular face, so I got a soft perm.

explain: '동그란 얼굴형', '갸름한 얼굴형'처럼 얼굴 윤곽을 나눠서 말할 때 써요. 안경이나 머리 모양을 고를 때 '얼굴형에 맞다', '얼굴형에 어울리다'라고 많이 해요.
explain_en: It is used to classify the outline of a face, as in '동그란 얼굴형' (round face shape) and '갸름한 얼굴형' (slim face shape). When choosing glasses or a hairstyle, people say '얼굴형에 맞다' or '얼굴형에 어울리다'.

examples.en: Today I want to eat something with a spicy, hearty broth.

examples.ko: 순두부찌개에 청양고추를 썰어 넣으니 얼큰한 맛이 두 배가 됐어요.
examples.en: After I sliced chili peppers into the soft tofu stew, the spicy kick doubled.

examples.ko: 이 짬뽕은 국물이 얼큰해서 속이 풀려요.
examples.en: This jjamppong has a spicy broth that soothes my stomach.
I ate kimchi stew that was boiled spicy and rich.

examples.ko: 비 오는 날에는 얼큰한 찌개가 생각나요.
examples.en: On rainy days I think of a spicy stew.

examples.ko: 얼큰한 맛에 땀이 났지만 계속 먹었어요.
examples.en: The spiciness made me sweat, but I kept eating.

explain: 그냥 매운 것이 아니라 맵고 시원하게 느껴지는 국물 맛에 주로 써요. 찌개, 탕, 국 같은 국물 요리에 잘 어울리고, 매운 과자나 매운 소스에는 보통 '맵다'를 써요.
explain_en: It is not just for anything spicy, but mainly for the spicy-yet-refreshing taste of a soup broth. It suits soup dishes like stews and '탕', while for spicy snacks or sauces people normally use '맵다'.

examples.en: I bumped into the door and my big toe swelled up.
My big toe hurts because of my new dress shoes.
There is a hole in the big toe part of my sock.
Try standing with your weight on your big toe.
My big toenail cracked, so I went to the hospital.
The baby plays with its big toe in its mouth.

explain: 손의 '엄지손가락'처럼 발에서 가장 굵은 발가락이에요. 가장 작은 발가락은 '새끼발가락'이라고 해요. 발가락은 '발톱', '발가락 양말'처럼 다른 말과도 붙여서 많이 써요.
explain_en: Like the '엄지손가락' on the hand, it is the thickest toe on the foot. The smallest toe is called '새끼발가락'. '발가락' also joins with other words, as in '발톱' (toenail) and '발가락 양말' (toe socks).

en: a couple of days ago; the other day

examples.en: I watched a movie with a friend a couple of days ago.
I just bought these clothes the other day and they're already too small.

examples.ko: 엊그저께 입학한 것 같은데 벌써 졸업이에요.
examples.en: It feels like I entered school just the other day, and now it's already graduation.

examples.ko: 엊그저께 비가 많이 와서 길이 젖어 있어요.
examples.en: It rained a lot a couple of days ago, so the road is still wet.
I still remember what happened a couple of days ago.
I called a couple of days ago but you didn't pick up.

explain: '엊그제'와 같은 말이고, 어제나 그제쯤 되는 가까운 과거를 말해요. '엊그제 같다'처럼 쓰면 시간이 정말 빨리 지났다는 느낌을 나타내요.
explain_en: It is the same word as '엊그제', and refers to the recent past around yesterday or the day before. Used as '엊그제 같다', it expresses a feeling that time has passed very quickly.
